title: The timeline of an hour-long edit scrolls, zooms and redraws at 120 Hz with hundreds of clips
goal: On a long edit the timeline is where a person spends their time, and it is the part most likely to slow down as clips pile up: every clip bar, thumbnail strip and waveform drawn again when anything moves. Make the timeline of the 60 minute reference edit, several hundred clips, scroll, zoom and follow a playing playhead at the display's 120 Hz, and keep an edit on it inside one frame.
notes: Fourth success item of video-perf ('the timeline scrolls and zooms at 120 Hz with hundreds of clips'). Depends on the speed walk task a-speed-walk-measures-the-long-reference-edit-th; if that walk's ranking says the timeline is not where the time goes, say so in the log and narrow this to what it measured. Precedents for building only what is on screen: the-layers-list-only-builds-the-rows-you-can-see, the-layers-panel-only-draws-thumbnails-for-the-r, keying-a-value-redraws-only-what-the-key-changes (all done). Timeline code: TimelineTrackRows.swift, ClipPiecesBar.swift (104 KB), TimelineDock.swift, SoundLane.swift; 23 app files read editorState.documentTimeMS. The playhead belongs on its own layer, not in the clip rows' bodies.
acceptance: Measured first with the speed walk on the 60 minute reference edit at Next defaults: frame times scrolling and zooming the timeline end to end, view bodies rebuilt per playback frame, and the longest main thread pass for trim, move, blade and undo. Numbers in the audit before any change.
Scrolling and zooming the 60 minute timeline: no frame over 8.3 ms on the main thread (120 Hz) in 95 percent of frames and none over 16 ms, measured by the speed walk.

While it plays with nothing being edited, only the playhead and what the playhead changes are rebuilt each frame: clip bars, thumbnails and waveforms off screen or unchanged are not built again (counted with ViewBuildMeter, the count in the audit before and after).
Trim, move, blade and undo on the 60 minute edit each finish within 16 ms on the main thread, as on the 6 minute one.
No change in what the timeline shows: the timeline walks that photograph it (cut, trim, transitions, key lanes) stay green. Perf numbers before and after in the audit; Scripts/test.sh passes.
Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not.

Pass 1 (2026-11-14). Found first: the speed walk timed the probe with the walk's own markers hung, about 29,000 AppKit views on the 60 min timeline (PanelTargetAnchor 4548, HoverTargetAnchor 2055, HelpAnchor 1621, ReadoutAnchor 1465, each with its host), which a person's app does not have. Speed measures now take the markers down (PlaytestHarness .speed -> takeTheMarkersDownForATimedStep(always: true)): 374 views. Numbers on the 60 min edit, markers down, before any timeline change: zoom in 736 ms a frame, zoom out 747, scroll 554. With markers (as the old walk read it): zoom 1225/1099, scroll 901, edits trim 833 / move 780 / blade 977 / undo 837 ms longest pass.

Pass 1 landed: (1) TimelineSight (PhotonzCore, tested): a lane builds only the clips, linked sounds, gaps, edit points, child marks, click ticks, blade and track-select targets within the window plus half a window each side, snapped to power-of-two steps so a slow scroll reuses the same lists; picked, trimmed and in-hand clips keep their views. (2) layer(id:) answers from an index kept in DocumentDerived once a document has been asked 16 times without a write (it was 13% of a zoom frame). (3) holdDrifts gathers the picture-only holds once per document instead of walking the document per bar. After, 60 min edit: zoom in 571 ms (p95 650), zoom out 580, scroll 50 ms (p95 59); edits trim 559 / move 492 / blade 696 / undo 713 ms; playing untouched 93 pictures in 3 s (full clock rate, was 70), clip bars built per picture 0 (also 0 before). 24 timeline walks green incl. speed-walk and an-editing-session-walk; Scripts/test.sh green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-14-timeline-hour-long-scroll-zoom.json.

Pass 2 (2026-11-14). Baseline re-measured at 602579415 (60 min edit, markers down): zoom in 567 ms/frame (only 38 frames, ~4x, in its 20 s), zoom out 588, scroll 50; edits trim 526 / move 534 / blade 683 / undo 704 ms. Floor experiment (throwaway switch): clip bars stubbed out -> zoom 24 ms; bars, edit points, ticks and zoom lanes all out -> 8.3 ms. So the cost was the bar views.

Pass 2 landed: a busy lane (24+ clips in sight, TimelinePaint in PhotonzCore, tested) paints its plain clips (fill, edge, name, picture fades, linked sound half with waveform, level line and fade diamonds) and its cuts (seams and transition bands, in the lane's own order) in two Canvas layers (TimelinePaintedClips.swift). A clip/cut picked, in a hand, trimmed, renamed, under the pointer (lane-wide onContinuousHover), or carrying anything the painting does not draw (pieces, still, badge, keys, drift, level points, sound badge, pictures along it, a hold on a band) stays its full view. Painted clips take a click, drag and right click (TimelinePaintedHands). Parity checked pixel by pixel against pre-change captures at Fit, 2x, 4x (<800 stray pixels of 765k). Gotchas: SwiftUI snaps view frames to pixels (snap minX/maxX), the band view is never narrower than its 12 pt glyph (centred), custom Tone ShapeStyles do not resolve in a Canvas (use .color(tone.color(scheme)) with the VIEW's colorScheme), a sub-pixel picture fade shade shows as a 1 px line only when pixel-rounding gives it width. After: zoom 50 ms median over all 240 frames (p95 229/244), scroll 50 (unchanged: pictures show there, still full bars), edits trim 192 / move 167 / blade 243 / undo 177 ms. New walk painted-clips-take-a-hand-walk (real click on a painted clip picks it). 11 timeline/reference walks + speed-walk + an-editing-session-walk green; Scripts/test.sh green.
